candidates.name: Lebanese Baked Kafta and Potatoes (Kafta bil Sanieh)
candidates.why: Sheet-pan tray bake: kafta pressed flat, potato and tomato layered on top, one sauce poured over. Scales to a full hotel pan and portions by weight. Every component is board-mapped. Confidence: page verified live via site listing; calorie figure is my estimate from the ingredient ratios, source has no nutrition panel.

candidates.name: Izmir Kofte (Turkish Meatballs Baked with Potatoes)
candidates.why: Oven casserole, no per-plate assembly. Beef plus potato plus rice easily clears 500 cal and 30g protein. All ingredients on the board. Near-dupe watch: same family as Sebzeli Kofte below, dedup should keep only one Turkish meatball-and-vegetable bake.

candidates.name: South African Bobotie (Curried Beef Custard Bake)
unmapped_flags: mango chutney (substitute: apricot jam or applesauce, both board-adjacent)
candidates.why: Explicit hunting-ground target. A single baked casserole with an egg custard top, ideal at 14 servings. Source verifies 293 cal for the bake alone at 6 servings; served over the traditional turmeric rice it lands near 560 cal with roughly 30g protein. Chutney is the only off-board item and swaps cleanly.

candidates.name: Ethiopian Berbere Ground Beef (Minchet Abish)
candidates.why: Explicit hunting-ground target and berbere-seasoning is already a tracked commodity. One-pot braise, holds and reheats well, portions by scoop over rice. Confidence: recipe page verified; calorie value is estimated (source lists no panel for the rice-served portion).

candidates.name: Japanese Soboro Don (Sweet Soy Beef and Egg Rice Bowls)
candidates.why: Explicit hunting-ground target. Beef soboro and seasoned egg both cook in big flat batches then get weighed over rice, which is exactly our portioning model. Eggs push protein well past 30g. Confidence: page fetched and confirmed as a real recipe; it publishes no nutrition, so calories are my estimate.

candidates.name: British Cottage Pie
candidates.why: Catalog has no shepherd's/cottage pie at all, which is a real gap for a budget-dinner site. Pure bake-and-divide, 100% board-mapped, cheap per serving. Confidence: source page verified; calories estimated from ingredient ratios.

candidates.name: Greek Moussaka
unmapped_flags: eggplant (no board commodity; the potato-heavy version of this dish is fully mappable)
candidates.why: Major cuisine gap: pastitsio is live but moussaka is not. Layered tray bake, cuts into clean squares at 14 servings. Only eggplant is off-board and many published versions are potato-only.

candidates.name: Albondigas en Chipotle (Mexican Meatballs in Chipotle Sauce)
candidates.why: Meatballs simmer in one pot of sauce and go over rice; scales linearly. chipotle-adobo is already tracked. Catalog has no albondigas of any kind. Confidence: page verified; calories estimated.

candidates.name: Sopa de Fideo con Carne Molida (Mexican Beef and Noodle Skillet)
candidates.why: Fideo maps to the board's pasta commodity; cooked thick (the stew-style version) it eats as a dinner, not a starter soup. One-pot, very cheap. Confidence: page verified; calories estimated because published versions vary from soupy to thick.

candidates.name: Pastel de Choclo (Chilean Beef and Corn Casserole)
candidates.why: Source publishes 537 cal and 35g protein per serving, so this qualifies on verified numbers rather than estimate. Corn-topped tray bake, every ingredient including olives and raisins is a tracked commodity.

candidates.name: Escondidinho de Carne (Brazilian Beef and Potato Bake)
unmapped_flags: cassava/yuca (the traditional topping; the widely published mashed-potato version is fully board-mapped)
candidates.why: Brazil is unrepresented in beef. Two-layer bake, cheesy top, portions by square. Use the potato-topped version and the whole thing maps. Confidence: page verified; calories estimated.

candidates.name: Kibbeh bil Sanieh (Lebanese Baked Kibbeh Tray)
unmapped_flags: fine bulgur #1 (no board commodity; it is the structural grain here and cannot be swapped without changing the dish)
candidates.why: Lean-beef-heavy tray bake, three flat layers, cuts into diamonds. Naturally very high protein because bulgur is a small fraction of the mass. Flagging bulgur honestly: without a board home its cost is unpriced, so this needs a call before it ships.

candidates.name: Kefta Mkaouara (Moroccan Meatball and Egg Tagine)
candidates.why: Explicit hunting-ground target (Middle Eastern/North African kofta). Eggs cooked into the sauce lift protein hard. One skillet, no assembly. Near-dupe watch: shares the meatballs-in-tomato-sauce shape with Albondigas en Chipotle, though the spice profile and the eggs make it a different dinner. Confidence: page verified; calories estimated.

candidates.name: Beef Maqluba (Palestinian Upside-Down Rice)
unmapped_flags: eggplant (optional layer; the cauliflower-and-potato version is fully board-mapped)
candidates.why: Single pot, layered and flipped, or simply scooped for meal prep. Rice plus beef puts it comfortably over 500 cal. Not a hashweh repeat: different structure, vegetables, and cooking method from the live Lebanese Hashweh. Confidence: page verified; calories estimated.

candidates.name: Pastelon (Puerto Rican Sweet Plantain and Beef Bake)
unmapped_flags: ripe plantains (no board commodity; they are the structural layer and cannot be substituted)
candidates.why: Layered lasagna-style bake, cuts and holds beautifully. Strong cuisine gap. Flagging plantains rather than quietly pricing them as bananas, which would be wrong on both cost and yield.

candidates.name: Karniyarik (Turkish Beef-Stuffed Eggplant Bake)
unmapped_flags: eggplant (no board commodity, and here it is the vessel, not a garnish)
candidates.why: Roasted-and-filled trays rather than plate-by-plate assembly, so it does scale, though it is the most assembly-heavy candidate in this slice. Include only if eggplant gets a board home; otherwise it is unpriceable.

candidates.name: Youvarlakia Avgolemono (Greek Beef and Rice Meatballs in Lemon Sauce)
candidates.why: Rice is built into the meatballs and the egg-lemon sauce adds protein, so this eats as a full dinner rather than a soup. Everything is board-mapped and cheap. Confidence: page verified; calories estimated, and portioning needs to be thick (less broth) to hold 500+ cal.

candidates.name: Kenyan Beef Pilau
unmapped_flags: green cardamom pods (whole-spice only; ground substitutes exist but cardamom has no board id)
candidates.why: One-pot spiced rice, absolutely built for batch cooking, and East African cuisine is entirely absent from the catalog. Chuck keeps the cost down versus cubed sirloin. Confidence: page verified; calories estimated.

candidates.name: Cantonese Beef, Tomato and Egg over Rice
candidates.why: A genuinely cheap protein-dense bowl: eggs plus beef over rice, every item board-tracked. Cooks in two big pans and gets weighed out. Confidence: page verified; calories estimated.

candidates.name: Cambodian Beef Lok Lak Rice Bowls
candidates.why: Southeast Asian black-pepper beef, no catalog equivalent. Stir-fries in batches and portions over rice. Chose this over Vietnamese bo luc lac deliberately: the two are near-duplicates and only one should ship. Confidence: page verified; calories estimated.

candidates.name: Pakistani Chapli Kebab Rice Bowls
unmapped_flags: dried pomegranate seeds/anardana (traditional souring agent; pomegranate-molasses is on the board and is a workable stand-in)
candidates.why: Patties, but sheet-pan bakeable in a single tray rather than fried to order, so it survives the batch test. Distinct from the live keema recipes: whole toasted spices, tomato in the mix, patty format. Confidence: page verified; calories estimated with rice.

candidates.name: Peruvian Tallarines Verdes con Carne (Green Spaghetti with Beef)
unmapped_flags: queso fresco (parmesan and cream-cheese are both board-tracked substitutes commonly used in US versions)
candidates.why: Peru is unrepresented and this is a pasta bake-adjacent dish that reheats well. Spinach-basil sauce, walnuts, and evaporated milk are all tracked commodities. Confidence: page verified; calories estimated for the beef version (source is the sauce-and-pasta base).

candidates.name: Korean Beef and Kimchi Fried Rice
unmapped_flags: kimchi (no board commodity; it is the defining ingredient and cannot be swapped)
candidates.why: gochujang and sesame-oil are already tracked, kimchi is not. Near-dupe watch: the catalog already has Ground Beef Fried Rice Bowls, so this only survives dedup if the kimchi/gochujang character is judged a different dinner. Confidence: page verified; calories estimated.

candidates.name: Chile Relleno Casserole with Ground Beef
candidates.why: The casserole form of a dish that is otherwise fried to order, which is exactly the adaptation the batch rule asks for. Egg-and-cheese custard means high protein without more meat. Fully board-mapped. Confidence: page verified; calories estimated.

candidates.name: Trinidadian Beef Pelau
unmapped_flags: pigeon peas (canned-black-beans / kidney-beans are the closest board items and are commonly substituted)
candidates.why: Caramelized-sugar one-pot rice, a genuine Caribbean gap. Chuck keeps it cheap. Confidence: page verified; calories estimated.

candidates.name: Korean Beef Japchae Noodle Bowls
unmapped_flags: sweet potato starch noodles/dangmyeon (no board commodity; rice-noodles is the nearest tracked item but changes the dish)
candidates.why: Mixes in one giant bowl and holds cold or warm, which is ideal meal-prep behavior. Everything but the noodle itself is tracked. Protein needs the beef ratio pushed up from the source's proportion to clear 25g.

candidates.name: Sichuan Ants Climbing a Tree with Beef
unmapped_flags: glass/bean thread noodles (no board commodity; rice-noodles is tracked and is a common substitution)
candidates.why: This source uses beef mince specifically, which suits our slice. One wok, noodles absorb the sauce, portions by weight. chili-crisp is already tracked. Confidence: page verified via search listing; calories estimated.

candidates.name: Kerala Beef Ularthiyathu (South Indian Beef Fry) Rice Bowls
unmapped_flags: curry leaves
fresh coconut slices (coconut-oil and coconut-milk-canned are tracked; sliced fresh coconut is not)
candidates.why: Pressure-cook then dry-roast, which is genuinely a batch method, and it is a completely different Indian dish from the two live keema recipes. Very high protein density because the sauce cooks off. Confidence: page verified; calories estimated.

candidates.name: Nikujaga (Japanese Beef and Potato Simmer)
unmapped_flags: dashi (chicken-broth or beef-broth substitutes cleanly and both are tracked)
candidates.why: Classic one-pot simmer, tastes better on day two, which is the meal-prep ideal. Distinct from the live Japanese Ground Beef Curry. Confidence: URL confirmed present via search index; I did not fetch the page body itself, and calories are estimated.

candidates.name: Loobia Polo (Persian Beef and Green Bean Rice)
unmapped_flags: saffron (optional; turmeric is tracked and is the standard budget substitute)
candidates.why: One-pot layered rice, fully board-mapped, and Persian beef is missing from the catalog. Verified numbers: source lists 461 cal and 17.7g protein per serving, so our version needs the beef raised from 1 lb to roughly 2 lb per 8 servings to hit the 25g protein bar. Flagging that explicitly rather than passing the source figure along.

candidates.name: Sebzeli Kofte (Turkish Meatball and Vegetable Stew)
candidates.why: One pot, all board-mapped, very cheap per serving. Near-dupe watch: overlaps Izmir Kofte (Turkish meatballs plus vegetables); dedup should keep whichever reads better, not both. Confidence: page verified; calories estimated.

candidates.name: Greek Bifteki with Lemon Potatoes
candidates.why: Sheet-pan: patties and potatoes roast in the same tray. Feta and lemon make it clearly Greek rather than a Salisbury steak repeat, but flagging that the live Salisbury Steak and Potato Bowls occupies the same patties-plus-potatoes shape and one of them may lose at dedup. Confidence: page verified; calories estimated.

candidates.name: Giouvetsi (Greek Beef and Orzo Bake)
candidates.why: Orzo maps to the board's pasta commodity. Braise then bake the pasta into the same dish, which is one of the most reliable 14-serving formats we have. Distinct from the live Pastitsio (no bechamel, chunk beef). Confidence: page verified; calories estimated.

candidates.name: Middle Eastern Beef, Spinach and Chickpea Stew
candidates.why: Verified numbers: 292 cal and 26g protein for the stew alone, so over rice it lands near 560 cal with protein intact. Seven ingredients, all board-mapped, frozen spinach keeps it cheap. One of the strongest cost-per-serving candidates in this slice.

candidates.name: Turkish Pasta with Garlic Yogurt and Spiced Butter
candidates.why: Verified 764 cal and 33g protein per serving from the source panel. Nothing like it in the catalog: yogurt sauce plus paprika butter instead of a red sauce. All board-mapped, and the yogurt layer is cheap protein.

candidates.name: Gyudon (Japanese Simmered Beef Rice Bowls)
unmapped_flags: dashi (broth commodities on the board substitute directly)
candidates.why: Simmer a big pot of beef and onion, hold it, ladle over rice. Optional egg pushes protein up. Thin-sliced beef prices against sirloin-steak or chuck-roast, both tracked. Confidence: page verified via site listing; calories estimated.

candidates.name: Cantonese Beef Rice Bowls
candidates.why: Steamed-style beef over rice, fully board-mapped, and unlike the live Beef Chow Mein or Ground Beef Fried Rice in both sauce and format. Confidence: page verified via site listing; calories estimated.

candidates.name: Beef and Mushroom Stir-Fry Rice Plate
candidates.why: Mushrooms are a tracked commodity and stretch the beef, which is good for cost per serving. Distinct from the two live beef-and-broccoli recipes. Confidence: page verified via site listing; calories estimated and this one is the closest to the 500 cal floor, so portioning must be generous.

candidates.name: Bistek Tagalog (Filipino Beef and Onions over Rice)
unmapped_flags: calamansi (limes and lemon-juice are both tracked and are the standard US substitute)
candidates.why: Five-ingredient braise that gets better held overnight. Filipino beef is missing from the catalog (only pork and chicken are represented). Confidence: page verified via site listing; calories estimated.

candidates.name: Filipino Beef Pares Rice Bowls
unmapped_flags: star anise (no board commodity; five-spice-powder is tracked and carries the same anise note)
candidates.why: Verified 719 cal and 54g protein per serving from the source panel, the highest-protein candidate in this slice. Source specifies brisket; chuck-roast is the tracked, cheaper cut and braises the same way. Slow-braise plus garlic rice, both batch formats.

candidates.name: Tortang Giniling (Filipino Beef and Potato Omelette Bake)
candidates.why: Traditionally pan-fried in rounds, but it bakes as one sheet-pan frittata, which is the adaptation that makes it batch-legal. Eggs plus beef is cheap protein, everything board-mapped. Confidence: page verified via site listing; calories estimated for the baked version.

candidates.name: Ghanaian Shoko (Beef and Spinach Stew)
unmapped_flags: scotch bonnet/habanero (jalapenos and cayenne-pepper are tracked substitutes)
candidates.why: West African beef is a real gap and this is a straightforward braise over rice. Spinach is tracked frozen and fresh. Confidence: page verified via site listing; calories estimated.

candidates.name: Nigerian Beef Stew over Rice
unmapped_flags: scotch bonnet (jalapenos / cayenne-pepper are tracked substitutes)
candidates.why: The base stew of Nigerian home cooking, all board-mapped including bouillon. Cooks in one pot at any volume. Confidence: page verified via site listing; calories estimated.

candidates.name: Soto Betawi (Indonesian Beef and Coconut Soup)
unmapped_flags: candlenuts (peanuts/almonds are tracked and are the usual substitute)
tamarind paste
candidates.why: coconut-milk-canned and lemongrass-paste are already tracked, which is most of the flavor base. Served over rice it eats as a dinner. Confidence: page fetched and confirmed real, uses brisket (swap to chuck-roast); the source publishes no nutrition so calories are estimated.

candidates.name: Picadinho de Carne (Brazilian Beef and Vegetable Stew)
candidates.why: Diced-beef stew served over rice and beans, entirely board-mapped. Different dish from Escondidinho above (stew versus bake) so both can survive. Confidence: page verified via site listing; calories estimated.

candidates.name: Kharcho (Georgian Beef and Walnut Rice Soup)
unmapped_flags: ground fenugreek
saffron (optional; ground-turmeric is tracked)
candidates.why: Verified 472 cal and 37g protein per serving from the source panel, so protein density is excellent even though calories sit just under 500; thickening it (more rice, less broth) clears the bar easily. Walnuts are a tracked commodity and carry the whole dish. Caucasus cuisine is entirely absent from the catalog.

candidates.name: Persian Kotlet (Beef and Potato Patties) with Rice
candidates.why: Potato-bound patties, sheet-pan bakeable, cheap because the potato stretches the beef. Fully board-mapped. Near-dupe watch: shares the patty-plus-potato shape with Greek Bifteki above; dedup should not keep both plus the live Salisbury Steak. Confidence: page verified via site listing; calories estimated.

candidates.name: Tunisian Harissa Coconut Beef Meatballs
candidates.why: Both signature ingredients, harissa-paste and coconut-milk-canned, are already tracked commodities, which is rare for a North African dish. One skillet of sauce, meatballs simmer in it. Confidence: page verified via site listing; calories estimated.

candidates.name: Moroccan Beef and Sweet Potato Tagine
unmapped_flags: dried apricots (raisins are tracked and are the common budget substitute)
candidates.why: Slow braise, all main components board-mapped, and chickpeas add cheap protein. No tagine or North African beef braise exists in the catalog. Confidence: page verified via site listing; calories estimated.

candidates.name: Pakistani Beef Kofta Curry
unmapped_flags: gram flour/besan (flour and cornstarch are tracked binders that work here)
candidates.why: Verified 572 cal and 30g protein per serving from the source panel. Yogurt-onion gravy, not a tomato curry, so it is a genuinely different dish from the two live keema recipes. Meatballs simmer in one pot.

candidates.name: Tteokgalbi (Korean Sweet Soy Beef Patties) Rice Bowls
candidates.why: Verified 406 cal and 23g protein for the patties alone at 4 servings; over rice that becomes roughly 640 cal and the protein holds. Fully board-mapped. Sheet-pan bakeable rather than grilled to order. Distinct from the live Korean Ground Beef Rice Bowls (patty format, glaze rather than stir-fry).

candidates.name: Korean Kimchi Stew with Beef
unmapped_flags: kimchi (no board commodity, and it is the defining ingredient)
firm tofu (no board commodity; optional here)
candidates.why: Slow-cooker format, which the catalog rewards, and gochujang is already tracked. Kimchi is the blocker: two candidates in this slice depend on it, so it may be worth registering as a commodity rather than dropping both. Confidence: page verified via site listing; calories estimated.

candidates.name: Xinjiang Cumin Beef Rice Bowls
unmapped_flags: Sichuan peppercorns (optional; black-pepper and red-pepper-flakes are tracked)
candidates.why: Heavy cumin and chili, nothing like the live Mongolian or beef-and-broccoli bowls. Stir-fries in batches. Confidence: page verified via search listing; calories estimated, and the cut should be repriced against chuck-roast if sirloin runs expensive that week.

candidates.name: Caribbean Curry Beef with Potatoes
unmapped_flags: scotch bonnet (jalapenos is the tracked substitute)
candidates.why: Caribbean curry is a distinct spice profile from the live Indian and Thai curries and the catalog has none. One-pot braise, potato stretches the beef. Confidence: page verified via site listing; calories estimated.

candidates.name: Carbonada (Chilean Beef, Corn and Squash Soup)
unmapped_flags: butternut/pumpkin squash (canned-pumpkin and sweet-potatoes are tracked stand-ins)
candidates.why: Hearty enough to be dinner when cooked thick, and dirt cheap because vegetables carry the volume. Confidence: page verified via site listing; calories estimated, and this is the lowest-calorie candidate in the slice, so it only qualifies with a generous portion and the rice included.
